notes: Process FMEA over the map's five steps (coffee-process-map s1-s5), rating the discrete failures that ride on top of the stable 8.4-minute baseline -- the chronic slowness itself is the baseline's common-cause story, not a failure mode. Ratings are anchor lookups with the between-anchor judgment calls argued here since rows carry no note field. Occurrence: re-pulls ran 10 of 120 sampled orders (~1 in 12), between the 1-in-20 (7) and 1-in-8 (8) anchors -- rated 7 because the tally counts only orders where rework was the dominant delay. Queue mix-ups and unheard name calls rated 6 (~1 in 80, burst-driven); mis-keys, buried cups, wrong finishes, and printer jams rated 5 (~1 in 400; the one tallied reprint in 120 sampled orders sits between the 5 and 6 anchors -- 5 chosen). The steam scald rated occurrence 2: one first-aid event recalled in roughly two semesters of peak service. Severity of the scald argued at 8, not 9: the credible event is a momentary first-aid burn with visible-steam warning, below the bar this team reserves for anchor 9's injury-level hazard -- and because severity is never ignorable at this level either, the row carries an action and owner regardless, so the board holds no unaddressed safety row. Detection 8 on the mix-up row: nothing checks cup against ticket between marking and name call. The highest RPN (288) is the drink-queue mix-up at the queue-to-station handoff; the severity-first view instead leads with the severity-8 scald at RPN 48 -- the two sorts disagreeing is the RPN limitation on display, and both rows get actions for their own reasons.

rows.failure_mode: Marked cups taken out of ticket order during a burst; two orders swap at the queue-to-station handoff
rows.effect: Drinks built against the wrong tickets -- both customers wait through a remake and the queue behind them stalls
rows.cause: Handwritten cup marks smear near the steam wand; grab order is whatever sits closest when the queue runs six-plus deep
rows.action: Replace handwritten marks with POS-printed sticky labels applied in ticket order; queue rail gets a marked front position so oldest cup is always the grab

rows.step_name: Take order and payment at register
rows.failure_mode: Order details keyed wrong at the register (size, milk, decaf)
rows.effect: Customer receives the wrong drink at handoff; the remake doubles that customer's wait
rows.cause: Peak-rush entry with abbreviated POS buttons; modifiers mistapped and unread
rows.action: Add a one-line read-back of size/milk/decaf to the register script during peak

rows.failure_mode: Steam wand contacts the barista's hand while juggling pitcher and portafilter in a rush
rows.effect: Barista scalds a hand -- a first-aid burn, and the station stops while it is treated
rows.cause: Wand parks angled into the work path; rush pace puts the pitcher hand across it
rows.action: Re-angle the wand to park outboard of the work path and add purge-and-park to the drink-build standard

rows.failure_mode: A marked cup gets buried mid-queue and its drink never starts until the customer asks
rows.effect: One customer waits ten-plus minutes and may walk away -- the VoC's vending-machine line made real
rows.cause: Cups nine deep in a class-break burst hide the oldest mark from view
rows.action: Covered by the queue-rail ticket-order fix (r-queue-mixup); name-call loop adds an oldest-mark sweep each cycle

rows.failure_mode: Shot pulls sour or channelled and is dumped, the drink re-started from dosing
rows.effect: That drink restarts and every cup behind it waits roughly two more minutes
rows.cause: Grind setting drifts after mid-peak hopper refills until the grinder is re-dialed
rows.action: Re-dial the grind after every hopper refill; refills logged on the check sheet so drift is visible

rows.step_name: Call name and hand off at pickup counter
rows.failure_mode: Name called once, unheard over peak noise; the finished drink strands on the counter
rows.effect: Drink cools while the recorded wait keeps running -- the VoC's 'nobody called my name' complaint
rows.cause: Single spoken call competes with music and grinder noise at peak

rows.failure_mode: Wrong syrup pumped or lid/sleeve missed on the finished drink
rows.effect: Drink comes back across the counter for a quick fix or remake
rows.cause: Syrup pumps unlabeled on the back row; finish happens mid-conversation at pickup

rows.step_name: Take order and payment at register
rows.failure_mode: Ticket printer jams and the order is re-rung
rows.effect: The order enters the drink queue late; one reprint tallied in the study (check-sheet E32)
rows.cause: Worn printer feed roller jams on multi-item tickets
